propagate.description: Whether the status change propagates to subaddresses.

type.description: Whether the process ended successfully or with an error.

CloseOutcome.description: Outcome of a process that has terminated.

bindings.description: Key chord → action (see Action) for this prompt.

input.description: The prompt's input: its content (what the user is typing, with the `selection`, the ghost-text `filigrane` and its `editability`) and its context (the marker text above the editor). Not to be confused with the cell's `submission` (CellConfiguration), what a cell shows was submitted.

focus.description:
If true, the prompt takes the focus (its tab shown, if hidden), as this configuration is applied: e.g. for a command that just changed the prompt's content, to hand it back to the user. Not kept: each configuration with it focuses the prompt once. (It overrides `background` for a new prompt.)

For a new cell, or a new process (the cell standing in for what it shows): it takes the focus as it appears, as a command's echo does (see CommandRequest's `id`): e.g. for a command submitted by another one, which buche didn't send. Only when the entry is created (and, as for a prompt, it overrides `background`).

kind.description: What the entry shows: a terminal, a frame (a GUI), or a prompt (the prompt fields, `bindings`, `input` and `request_id`, then apply). What it is sent must suit it (text for a terminal, the rest for a frame). An entry cannot change kind: a kind other than the one it has is an error.

request_id.description: For a prompt: set when this message is the *echo* answering a parse (the highlight a keystroke triggered): it repeats that parse's `request_id`, and is only applied while that parse is still the latest for this prompt — a stale echo (the user typed on in the meantime) is dropped. Absent (the norm) for authoritative configurations: the fresh prompt, the submit reset, history navigation.

submission.description: What was submitted: the command text, and the context it was submitted in (e.g. the prompt it was typed at: host, path, branch). The context, when present, is shown above the echo box in the accent color. A configuration may give either subfield alone; the other keeps its current value. Echos are read-only, always: the content's `editability` (see InteractiveStructuredText) defaults to "readonly" here and any value has no effect (only "readonly" is supported for echos for now).

label.description: The cell/tab label: styled text (its parts' styles can set the font, e.g. "mono" or "sans"), or a plain string.

icon.description: The cell/tab icon, shown before the label. Explicit null removes it.

id.description: The id of the user command this echo answers (repeated from the "command" request's `id`). The interface uses it to give the focus to the echo's element when it appears.

sticky.description: If true, keep the focus on the cell when its process ends.

background.description: If true, do not automatically focus the cell or prompt.

ephemeral.description: If true, the element showing this entry (the cell's box, and with it its tab) is removed when the entry is marked done or error. Prompts already go away when their process ends.

grow.description: If true, the cell takes whatever height its content needs in a scroll stream, instead of being capped (its own scrollbar past the cap): e.g. a chat transcript, read by scrolling the stream itself.

status.description: Switch the entry (and what is under it) between running and standby. A standby entry is a temporary interface the user may be done with: it is killed by a clear, like spent cells are removed, or once it has stayed scrolled out of view for a while. Ignored once the entry is done or errored.

zone.description: Which zone to put the element in.

anchor.description: Address of the entry the zone is relative to (e.g. "right": right of it), instead of the one `from` implies (its closest ancestor showing something: for a command, the prompt it came from). E.g. a command's output beside the cell the command was performed on. An entry that shows nothing itself (a process) stands for what it shows. Like `zone`, only heeded when the entry is created; ignored if nothing shows there.

ConfigureMessage.description:
Declares (or reconfigures) an entry. It carries the cell configuration (label, color, `ephemeral`, ...), which the entry's views show too, and says where the entry goes (`zone`, relative to `anchor`).

With a `kind`, the entry shows something itself: a terminal, a frame or a prompt (see  {@link  ViewConfiguration.kind } ); the first time, it takes the place of its parent's placeholder if it can. Without, it is a process, or any non-visual parent of cells and prompts: the first time, it gets a placeholder (`<from>.?`), an empty cell placed in `zone` that stands in for the first cell or prompt the entry shows (see `Buche.claim`), and takes its input meanwhile.

Action.description: What a key binding, or a clicked part, does. The terminal only reads `freeze`, and sends the action to the driver (see CommandRequest), which carries it out. A string is a command line: short for `{command: <it>}`.

freeze.description: If true, the prompt's content is frozen as the action fires.

inherit.description: If true, the binding also works in every cell under the prompt's address (the cells of the commands run from it, and theirs...); the closest prompt's inherited binding for a key wins (and in a prompt, its own bindings). Fired from such a cell, the command request's `anchor` is that cell's address, and its text and selection are empty (not the prompt's).

CommandAction.description: A command line for the driver to run (as if submitted, but leaving the prompt and its history alone).

freeze.description: If true, the prompt's content is frozen as the action fires.

inherit.description: If true, the binding also works in every cell under the prompt's address (the cells of the commands run from it, and theirs...); the closest prompt's inherited binding for a key wins (and in a prompt, its own bindings). Fired from such a cell, the command request's `anchor` is that cell's address, and its text and selection are empty (not the prompt's).

BuiltinAction.description: One of the driver's built-in actions (e.g. coquille's submit, next...).

editability.description: Editability status of the text. Defaults to "editable" in a prompt, "readonly" in an echo (only "readonly" is supported in echos for now). "frozen" — set when a freezing binding fires — acts like "readonly", but is styled differently to denote a temporary condition.

filigrane.description: Ghost text displayed next to the text as a completion suggestion.

action.description: Fired when the part is clicked, as a key binding would be (the driver gets the same command request). Only in a prompt's context; elsewhere the part is shown as if it had none.

style.description: Style (an accent: colour, bold, italic, font...). Absent or null: unstyled.

TextPart.description: A run of text in a single style.

action.description: Fired when the part is clicked, as a key binding would be (the driver gets the same command request). Only in a prompt's context; elsewhere the part is shown as if it had none.

spacer.description: How the spacer is sized: "grow" takes the remaining space.

SpacerPart.description: Blank space between parts. A "grow" spacer takes all the space left over on the line, shared with the other grow spacers: e.g. one spacer pushes what follows it to the right edge. Ignored in an editable prompt.

action.description: Fired when the part is clicked, as a key binding would be (the driver gets the same command request). Only in a prompt's context; elsewhere the part is shown as if it had none.

style.description: Style applied to every part in the group (an accent). Absent or null: none.

GroupPart.description: Parts taken together: the group's style applies to each of them (under their own styles: e.g. a group in "bold" with a part in "red" shows it in bold red), and its action covers them all (one click target over the whole run). Spacers only take effect at the top level: in a group, they are ignored.

start.description: Inclusive starting position of the selection

end.description: Exclusive ending position of the selection

StructuredText.description: Text made of parts, shown one after the other. In an editable prompt, the first part absorbs text the user inserts at the very beginning, and the last part text the user appends (so a single part styles everything typed).

ViewKind.description: What a cell shows, as a driver declares it: a terminal, a frame (an HTML page the driver drives: a GUI), or a prompt.

Icon.description: A cell/tab icon: an image, or a character drawn in a font, on an optional coloured circle or square.

mimetype.description: The image's MIME type, e.g. "image/png" or "image/svg+xml".

data.description: The image: base64 when `encoding` is "base64", else the text itself (SVG).

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64", or null/absent for text.

mask.description: If true, only the image's shape counts: it is painted in the current text colour (like a glyph), e.g. for a monochrome SVG.

text.description: The character (or a few) to draw.

font.description: Font family: a CSS font-family list, or a keyword (mono, sans, serif, cursive).

color.description: Style of the character (an accent: colour, bold, italic...).

background.description: Background colour of the shape behind the character (none if absent).

GlyphIcon.description: An icon drawn as a character.

error_type.description: Class/kind of the error, e.g. the exception type.

ErrorMessage.description: An error reported by the process

id.description: The library's id, the host part of its URLs: 16 to 63 characters in `[a-z0-9-]`. Whoever knows it can load the library, so it must be unguessable. An id is bound to its files: declaring it again with different files is refused.

files.description: The files, by path in the library (e.g. `"js/main.js"`).

LibraryMessage.description:
Declare a library: files served to GUI cells at `lib://<id>/<path>`, which can reference each other by relative URLs. The driver sending it is the library's authority: it vouches for the files (a shell checks that the process declaring them could read them), and supplies their content on request (`library_fetch`, answered by `library_content`) — except for the files whose content comes with the declaration. See src/library.ts.

Handled by the host running the drivers (src/drivers.ts), not the terminal.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the file's content, lowercase hex. Required without `content`; checked against it otherwise.

mimetype.description: MIME type the file is served with.

content.description: The content, inline, encoded as `encoding` says.

LibraryFile.description: A file of a declared library (see  {@link  LibraryMessage } ): its hash, the authority (the declaring driver) supplying the content on request; or its content itself, which needs no authority.

content.description: The content, encoded as `encoding` says (absent on error).

error.description: Why the content can't be supplied.

LibraryContentMessage.description: The answer to a `library_fetch` request: the content of a library file, or why it can't be had (the file is gone, or changed since it was declared). Handled by the host running the drivers (src/drivers.ts).

propagate.description: Whether the cells under `from` are reset too (default: true).

ResetMessage.description: Start the cells at and under `from` over, blank: a frame throws its GUI away for a fresh iframe, with no DOM, script state, handlers or cached resources left from the old one (send them again), and keeps the focus if the old one had it; a terminal (or a placeholder's) is cleared, screen and scrollback. What was done (or failed) runs again: a process that ended is started over (its driver closes it again when it ends). Prompts are left alone. It creates nothing: only the cells that exist are reset, and an address with nothing at it is ignored. E.g. a program restarting its child resets its own address (`["$proc"]`) to reset whichever views the child had.

message.description: Message to send to the cell.

code.description: JavaScript to execute. Evaluated as an expression when `response_id` is set (the value is sent back); as statements otherwise.

selector.description: CSS selector of the targets; `code` runs once per target, with `this` bound to it.

response_id.description: If set, the GUI responds with a `response` carrying the result (or error).

mode.description: How to inject the content; defaults to "append".

selector.description: CSS selector of the injection targets; defaults to the document body.

content.description: HTML to inject (scripts in it are re-created so they execute).

schemas.description: Schema spec (e.g. `"buche:plain"`) -> handler source for `data` payloads.

request_id.description: Correlates with the GUI's original resource request; when absent, the command pre-pushes the resource into the GUI's cache under `path`.

path.description: Resource path (cache push when there is no `request_id`).

content.description: Resource body; text or base64 depending on `encoding`.

response_id.description: Correlates with the request (`buche.request`, or an `exec` with a `response_id`) this answers.

value.description: Result value of a successful request.

error.description: Error description of a failed request.
